name: CA-43
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans 27 points Democratic, one of the bluest House seats in the country
Maxine Waters is a long-serving incumbent with a huge fundraising edge ($1.1M raised vs $15K)
Challenger Cristian Morales has essentially no campaign, with only $539 cash on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97%
model.rationale: The district's 27-point Democratic lean, Waters' incumbency, and an overwhelming financial asymmetry leave the Republican challenger with no realistic path; prediction markets confirm near-certain Democratic retention.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or late external shock could narrow the race, and nothing in the current evidence points to one.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 43rd District, centered in southern Los Angeles County, is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of 27 points toward Democrats. Maxine Waters, the longtime incumbent, advanced to the general election and is seeking another term. Her Republican challenger, Cristian Morales, has run a minimal campaign, reporting about fifteen thousand dollars raised and under six hundred dollars on hand, while Waters has raised more than one million dollars and holds a large cash advantage.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent. The combination of the district's heavy Democratic lean, Waters' incumbency and financial dominance, and the challenger's lack of resources makes an upset highly unlikely. The seat rates as Safe Democratic, with Waters expected to win by a wide margin in November.
